Q: Codeigniter pass a id to controller from view A:

Well, hidden inputs will work, and there may be another workaround that once you redirected to the method and use your id value i.e. get data from database, redirect again to another controller method with the clean URL you need.

Q: Link to a Controller function with parameter from a View (CodeIgniter) A:

There seems to be a typo in the string concatenation in your PHP code and you'll need a slash between your controller name and the first parameter. Perhaps it will work to use:

site_url("session/enter/" . $session_item['id'])

... rather than a + sign between the two strings.

Q: Redis server in Docker container with Nginx and redis_pass A:

Is there anything in the log files?

I'd recommend to enable debug log feature by recompiling both nginx and module to get more details in a error.log file.

In case of an issue with ngx_http_redis module, please go ahead and raise an issue for the project, thank you.

Q: What does a colored dot in the Explorer View in VS Code mean? A:

The red dot in the explorer tab is called a problem decoration. See also the related problems.decorations.enabled setting. The red colour is typically for error-level problems (yellow typically for warning-level, blue typically for info-level, but it can vary based on your colour theme).

Taking a look at your screenshot, you have a whole heck-ton of problems in your source code (113 errors, 5 warnings).

To get rid of the problem decorations, I'd suggest to actually fix those problems. Open up those files and you'll see red squiggly underlines where the problems are, and hover over them to see what the problem is, and then fix the described problem.

You can view an overview of all problems in the Problems Panel, which you can open with the View: Toggle Problems command in the command palette, or View > Problems in the menu bar.

The fact that you can run your program successfully probably means that you just haven't yet properly configured IntelliSense in your project. It's impossible to know what you're missing without more info. It might help you to read https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/languages/java.

A really stupid and bad way to get rid of those decorations in the Explorer View is to put "problems.decorations.enabled": false in your settings.json file. I don't recommend that. Fix the problems.

Q: How to use LINQ Distinct() with multiple fields A:

product.Select(m => new {m.CategoryId, m.CategoryName}).Distinct();

Hi

I know this is an old post but, if someone gets here searching for a solution (like me) since .NET6 there is an Enumerable.DistinctBy Method that can easily solve this kind of requirements.

I'm using .Net8 and I can use the value tuple to indicate the distinct attributes.

So.. In the op example it would be:

var distinctResult =  product.Select(x => new { x.CategoryId, x.CategoryName })
                .OrderBy(x => x.CategoryId)
                .ThenBy(x => x.CategoryName)
                .DistinctBy(x => (x.CategoryId, x.CategoryName ))
                .ToList();

I used the Op anonymous approach .. but in my case (as I already had my list) I just needed to sanitize the list to return:

return new AppSuccessResponse<IReadOnlyList<KeyValueItem>>(
    itemList
        .OrderBy(x => x.Name)
        .ThenBy(x => x.Value)
        .DistinctBy(x => (x.Name, x.Value))
        .ToList());

Hope it helps someone
